newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic daily power rallies on cold snap.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic daily power rallies on cold snap.

text.p: Day-ahead prices of wholesale electricity in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic rallied Thursday on forecast of temperatures plummeting overnight with the arrival of an arctic blast.
"It was all over the place," said an East Coast broker, referring to daily power trading in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district.

Firm, peak PJM electricity for Friday (excluding transmission costs) reportedly changed hands in a very wide range from $35.00-$50.00 a megawatt hour (MWh). Firm, peak power scheduled for Friday was last quoted at $45.00-$50.00, up about $15 from Wednesday's range.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Friday delivery rose $2 to $18.00-$20.00 from Wednesday's $16.00-$18.00 range.
Today's hourly PJM prices peaked in the mid-$20.00 area, well below Wednesday's high of $31.00.

Friday temperatures in the PJM region were predicted to plunge 10-20 degrees Fahrenheit from today's levels, peaking in the teens to 20s range during the day and sinking to the single digits and teens at night. Extended outlook showed PJM weather would moderate to near seasonal levels by Wednesday.
Despite the surge in daily prices, forward PJM values were flat to lower from Wednesday's levels amid falling NYMEX natural gas futures.

As of 1211 EST, the February Henry Hub gas contract dropped 25.1 cents to $3.360 per million British thermal units on profit-taking and outlook of warmer weather in the eastern half of the country next week.
PJM deliveries for the five business days next week were still offered near $33.00.
February PJM electricity was quoted at $29.75-$30.00, slightly lower than Wednesday's $29.90-$30.30 after several trades at $29.90.
March PJM electricity slipped to $24.75-$25.00 from Wednesday's $24.90-$25.20.
PJM deliveries April and May held steady at $22.50-$22.75, while June prices remained in the $25.10-25.35 range.
July/August PJM electricity edged down to $31.25-$31.40 from $31.35-$31.65 Wednesday.
Swing natgas prices at the Philadelphia city gate jumped in anticipation of the cold snap, up 75 cents from Wednesday to $5.25/mmBtu.
